messages:
Amanda: Heads up — after the model onboarding to v3.4.0 we saw a p99 spike on the staging runtime for long-chat traffic. Noticed during the canary rollout.
perf-ci: CI perf job failed on staging-inference: p95 increased from 63ms -> 142ms for the long_seq suite. See job 2026-03-xx.
Juan: Ugh. Did we change tokenizer or default seq config in the checkpoint?
Sasha: The model artifact includes a tokenizer update that pads with <|eos|> at the end instead of 0. That might change KV cache prefix lengths and kernel selection heuristics.
Kevin: Quick check: kernel selector logs show fallback to generic attention-kernel for some sequences. Kernel mismatch + quantize path fallback could explain the latency.
Amanda: I ran a profile on a failing worker. Attaching snippet: ```
profile summary:
  avg_token_latency: 11.2ms -> 20.8ms
  p95_token_latency: 58.3ms -> 127.9ms
  kv_cache_hit_rate: 91% -> 62%
  batching_utilization: 0.78 -> 0.54
hotspots:
  - kv_cache.lookup (saturating LRU) +18% cpu
  - attention_kernel.generic (fallback) +42% cpu
```
Juan: kv_cache_hit_rate drop is suspicious. If tokenizer adds eos/pad tokens different from previous, cache keys won't match prefix-hashes. Did the model change tokenizer_type or pad_token_id?
Sasha: Yes, pad_token_id moved from 0 -> 50256 implicitly in the new vocab. The model conversion script didn't set tokenizer.override_pad_id. config.json diff: ```
- "pad_token_id": 0
+ "pad_token_id": 50256
```
perf-ci: Bisect hint: regressions introduced between merge 0b3f9a5 (tokenizer update) and merge a1c2d3e (quantize conversion).
Kevin: I ran a local bisect across those two commits. The perf cliff lines up exactly with the tokenizer commit. When I force pad_token_id=0 during serve, p95 returns to baseline.
Amanda: So root cause: tokenizer pad/eos change caused prefixes to be different, reducing KV cache hits, increasing runtime attention fallback + worse batching.
Juan: Proposed mitigations: 1) Revert the tokenizer change in the staging release, 2) Add a runtime compatibility shim that normalizes pad/eos ids when computing KV cache keys, 3) Add a canary in CI that checks kv_cache_hit_rate delta on onboarding. Thoughts?
Sasha: Agreed. For short term I'd prefer (2) + a hotfix to config normalization — less disruptive than full revert. We can land revert if we hit prod.
Kevin: I have a small shim patch that maps pad_token_id in tokenizer meta to the previous pad id during PSK (prefix-hash) compute. Unit tests included. Patch: ```
// normalize pad for kv key
if (token.meta.pad_token_id != expected_pad) {
  token.meta.pad_token_id = expected_pad;
}
```
Amanda: Can you open a PR and mark it hotfix? Tag me + eng-oncall. Also add an integration test that simulates a long_prefix workload to assert kv_cache_hit_rate >= 85%.
Juan: I'll add a CI perf job that runs minimal inference trace and asserts no >20% regression on p95 across onboarding. Add to perf gating.
infra-bot: Route override applied: routed model v3.4.0 -> fallback variant v3.3.8 for canary in region us-east-1 (temporary). :white_check_mark:
Sasha: Re: kernel selection — we should also make the selector more robust to small vocab id shifts. I'll file a follow-up to consider hashing token spans rather than raw ids.
Amanda: Nice work triaging. PRs: #4021 (kv-shim), #4022 (ci-canary-check). Plan: ship kv-shim to staging first, monitor kv_cache_hit_rate and p95 for 2 rollouts, then decide on global rollout.
Kevin: Deploying kv-shim to staging now. Will post perf diff in 15m.
perf-ci: Perf job queued for staging-run-789.
Amanda: Thanks everyone. Keep updates here. :rocket:
